lines.text: The night train had one rule, printed on a card in every sleeper berth.
If the train stops between stations after midnight... keep your curtain closed.
I left mine open to watch the snow... and fell asleep to the rocking of the wheels.
I woke to silence. The train had stopped. Outside... just snow, and black pines.
Then, at the far end of the car, the door slid open.
Slow footsteps came down the aisle. And one by one... the curtains scraped open.
Something was looking into every berth.
The footsteps stopped outside mine. I gripped my curtain shut... and didn't breathe.
At last, they moved on. And the wheels began to turn.
In the morning, everyone in my car was there. Nobody missing.
The porter smiled when I told him. Good. It can't open a closed curtain.
Then I remembered. When I fell asleep... my curtain was open.
So who closed it? Behind me, under the blanket, something cold whispered... I did.
